Messages.Author: Ben Peal
Messages.Body:
.

Heya! I just got back from Europe, where I had a blast at the EC, as
well as hanging out in Munich, Vienna, Budapest, and Bratislava.

Many thanks to Carl Pilhatsch and the 2002 EC Team for hosting a
fantastic weekend! I had a ton of fun meeting and playing with
everyone! Congrats to Dave Bastijn and Stephane Lavrut for their
wins at the EC and Qualifier, respectively, as well as to those
who won the side events!

Random comments on the events:

Cool venue! Definitely the nicest place in which I've played a
tournament. I've heard some gripes about the cost of the events,
but for that venue I think it was money well spent.

I found the judging to be very good, with the judges being very
available, and their decisions to be fair. I think they handled
the discrepancies with the decklists in the Qualifier in a fair
and game-friendly manner. I really liked the decision to have
players leave the room after completing a round during the EC,
as it helped a little bit to mitigate scouting, and it did a ton
to keep the playing areas quiet (a big plus!).

There's been some talk of possible collusion in the finals of
the qualifier, but this outside observer got the impression that
Stephane's predator was intimidated by a player of the caliber
of Stephane. It was certainly a very dumb time to be intimidated,
and I hope that Noel (?) learns his lesson. I mean, c'mon, it's
the final round of a major tournament...no sense in being timid.
You were good enough to get that far, so you've got a shot at
winning. Go for it.

European Edge technology lags far behind American Edge technology.

You can bitch all you want about an irresposible Malk stealth
bleeder winning the championship, but the fact of the matter is
that it was a good choice for the event. You needed 2 GW and
8.5 VP to make the finals, so you either have to have a monster
3-win day, or you have to roll the dice with a mega-offense deck
and hope to score big. Dave rolled the dice and scored big. I
got 1 GW and 4 VP with the Wall of Doom. Oops. Then again, I
can't really bitch about a Malk stealth-bleeder winning a
championship. ;)

I agree with Sten During that the country that hosts the EC should
have its national qualifier well before the EC, with an additional
last-chance qualifier the day before the EC.

I would have liked for there to have been side events on Saturday,
to give those who were already qualified something to do instead of
the qualifier, event attendance records be damned. ;)

More signs at the venue indicating that, yes, we've found the right
place, and that the event is on such-and-such floor in such-and-such
room.

Daaaaaamn...trading was fun...You just showed up where people were
trading and you were trading non-stop...fun fun fun...

Again, I was honored to have met everyone. I've said it before, and
I'll say it again: I'm consistently impressed by the caliber of
people who play this game.

All in all, I had a truly fantastic time. Carl and the team ran
a world-class event, and I very much look forward to attending future
ECs!

Special thanks to Monica, Rui, Skaffen, Markus, and Thomas Gescwgowifwe
of Munich...Carl, Stephan, and Helga of Vienna...Gabor and Peter of
Budapest...and Martin and PK of Bratislava...for letting me crash at
their flats or showing me around town. The players' network for this
game totally rocks. :)

- Ben Peal, Prince of Boston
fu...@mindstorm.com

Messages.Author: Markus Schlein
Messages.Body:
Ben Peal schrieb:

> I would have liked for there to have been side events on Saturday,
> to give those who were already qualified something to do instead of
> the qualifier, event attendance records be damned. ;)

I think this is a very important point. Especially when it comes to
qualification for Sunday. I don't know if somebody already mentioned it,
but I think this was a problem that occurred to some players. I am
talking about the way the qualified players effected the way the games
went on Saturday.

There was a strong difference in the way the qualified players and the
non-qualified players played. Since the GW-rule was invented we saw a
decline in VP-splitting and everyone played more for their own interest.
That was not the case on every table at the EC. I saw players making
deals like "I'm already qualified, I'll let you have the GW." I also
benefited from this phenomenon, as my prey offered me a withdrawal in
the last game, since he was already qualified. Another example was, that
someone (qualified) called the great beast in one game. There is no
question that this is absolutely legal and fun to play, but I can not
assume that this person was after the goal of maximizing his VP.

What I want to say is that in the final qualifier the already qualified
players should not be allowed to play, since some of those spoil the
extreme affords of the non-qualified. This makes the final one totally
different from other qualifiers and much harder to qualify there. This
should be changed. What do you think?

> Again, I was honored to have met everyone. I've said it before, and

> I'll say it again: I'm consistently impressed by the calibre of

> people who play this game.

Me too. It was so cool to meet and play with those folks from this NG.
Having Ben as my Predator in round 1 was great. Thanks to Ben, Jeff, LSJ
and all of you for being there.

> All in all, I had a truly fantastic time. Carl and the team ran
> a world-class event, and I very much look forward to attending future
> ECs!

Absolutely true. Thanks to the organisation team it was a world class
event. I am looking forward to see all of you again next year in Germany. ;)

-Markus

I really suffered from this phenomenon. For example the 1st game : One guy
lays down one Anarch Revolt after the other. He gets ousted first (by his
own Anarch Revolts) and the lucky guy who drew a Minion Tap swept the table.
Is this fair ? I do not think so. Did he try to maximize his chances of
winning. Not at all.

And if you are trying to qualify this is EXTREMELY frustrating. Which such a
starting round you can even give up after Round 1.
The Problem is not that I lost, the problem is that I did not have the
slightest change to fight for the victory because someone chose to ruin the
game because he does not have to win. I think for a tournament the main
focus of the players should be the same. In a Storyline event everybody
tries to have fun and make a quote which will end up on a V:TES card ;-). In
an EC tournament everybody tries to collect GWs. In a qualifier the day
before the championship we have a very mixed field with people who are
decktesting, having fun, trying to qualify and even some who do not have a
specific goal at all. This does not mix very well.

My suggestion would be the following :

- The country which holds the EC has it´s own national qualifier way before
the EC. Probably another city than the one which is having the EC should be
considered.
- The day before the EC there is an international qualifier which is only
open for people who are not allready qualified. There should be some side
events for those.
- The alternative qualifying slots / participants scheme suggested by
Andreas Nusser should be used. This way we have the attendance record on the
EC and not on the qualifier :-). Aside from the fact that this is fairer for
the countries with large V:TES communities or strong foreign attendance.

> Absolutely true. Thanks to the organisation team it was a world class
> event. I am looking forward to see all of you again next year in Germany.
;)

Hopefully! The EC might end up somewhere else ...

Messages.Author: Joshua Duffin

"Johannes Walch" <joha...@scram.de> wrote in message

> own Anarch Revolts) and the lucky guy who drew a Minion Tap swept the
table.
> Is this fair ? I do not think so. Did he try to maximize his chances of
> winning. Not at all.

This is true as far as it goes, but this will *always* be possible
(that there are people who aren't "trying as hard as they could"
to win) in tournaments, and I don't think it's feasible to try to
legislate against it. If you think certain decktypes tend to make
other people win more often than they win themselves (and I would
agree with that), what are you going to do, force people not to
play those decktypes? People who aren't already qualified might play
decks like that too, you know (and do!).

You're right that people who are qualified don't even have the same
incentives as people who aren't in qualifier tournaments. And it
was for that reason that LSJ said, a year or so ago, that the
solution would obviously be to not allow qualified players to
compete in qualifier tournaments. A lot of people didn't want that
to happen, though, because they wanted to be able to play in the
"high-level competition" environment of the qualifiers even if they
had already qualified at an earlier event. So they didn't make
such a rule.

Maybe they should, but I really doubt that it would solve the
problem of people playing erratically or "incorrectly",
or selecting decks that you don't think are good choices.

> My suggestion would be the following :
>
> - The country which holds the EC has it´s own national qualifier way
before
> the EC. Probably another city than the one which is having the EC should
be
> considered.

I agree that this is a good idea just because the "last-chance
qualifier" isn't really going to draw only (or even mainly) from
the host country/region. So the host country should have a
qualifier that's "really its own".

> - The day before the EC there is an international qualifier which is only
> open for people who are not allready qualified. There should be some side
> events for those.

I think having side events can be a good idea, but if qualified
people are going to be excluded here, they should probably be
excluded in all qualifier tournaments after they become qualified.
(This results, in theory, in qualifiers getting "easier" as it
gets later in the year, as LSJ has written in the past. And it
annoys people who would like to play in qualifiers even after
becoming qualified. But those may be acceptable issues, I don't
know.)

> - The alternative qualifying slots / participants scheme suggested by
> Andreas Nusser should be used. This way we have the attendance record on
the
> EC and not on the qualifier :-). Aside from the fact that this is fairer
for
> the countries with large V:TES communities or strong foreign attendance.

I think a method like that (top 1/4 of participants qualify, or
something along those lines) might be good, sure.

It's not necessarily obvious that the Continental Championships
should be the largest tournaments of the year, though. The
concept behind them is that they are invitationals designed to
have the best players competing for the title of "best of the
best".

Josh

not a continental soldier

Team Rules (12 Player)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

TOURNAMENT STRUCTURE

1. DEFINE TEAMS
a. Receive Team assignation (Randomly)
b. Players Choose a Starter (from their Team) for Tourney Play
c. Players have 5 minutes to familiarize themselves with contents
d. Teams are defined as follows;

Team A: Camarilla (A1, A2, A3, A4)
Team B: Independent (B1, B2, B3, B4)
Team C: Sabbat (C1, C2, C3, C4)

2. DRAFT

a. Each player receives 4 boosters for purpose of draft
b. Split players into pods as per draft seating chart.
c. Players open their first pack (simultaneously) and may choose one
card
d. Pass the booster to the player on your left
e. Repeat until all cards from booster are gone.
f. Each player opens next booster
g. Repeat from step b, except step c will have booster passed in
direction
opposite of previous alignment (right instead of left for instance)

a. All crypts must be constructed 75% of a chosen clan
b. Grouping rules are in effect
c. 12 Vampires in Crypt, no more - no less
d. 75 Cards in Library, no more - no less
e. Players have 40 minutes to construct play decks
f. Players may NOT trade cards with their team members
g. All cards not included in decks go into the "Coffin"
h. Each Pod/table is to ensure that the proper # of cards end up in
the "Coffin"

4. TOURNAMENT RESOLUTION

a. Games will run with 3x Two Hour Rounds, NO Final round
b. Winning Team is defined by total number of Tournament Points gained
by all team members at the end of 3 rounds.

12 Starters (1 per player), with 2 Starters in excess

1 Box Camarilla Edition Precons (6 Starters)
1 Box V:TES Combo Starter Box (8 Starters)*
* No official word what exactly these are yet, but guessing 4 Sabbat &
4 Independent PreCons

For seating, I recommend handing out 3x5 cards labelled A1,B1,C1, and
so on. Players then should write their name on the 3x5 card, and
judges can use it for keeping track of seating, VP's, and Tournament
Points.

You may also want to add an additional $5 per person and have food
delivered for just after the 2nd round of play. This tends to keep
players in one place, and the event running timely.

The idea of the "Coffin" is to discourage Rare-Drafting somewhat, and
gives a perk to the player with the highest cumulative Tournament
Points.

There will be some seating redundancy, though players should never
find themselves seated next to someone they've already played against.

Independent Clan starters aren't quite as good as the Sabbat pre-cons
(and possibly the Camarilla Edition pre-cons). They gain a slight
advantage by having more transfers overall.

I think it's probably unavoidable that the size of tournament
(really, any "fact" about a tournament) can favor certain deck-
types. Any scoring system you could choose will be better for
some kinds of decks than for others. If you scrapped the VP
system and said "last person standing always wins the game,
no matter how many VPs they had", that would make "wall" decks
a lot "better" in tournaments. Similarly, an 8-person tournament
is probably better for rush combat decks than a 50-person
tournament, both because it doesn't need as many game wins to
make the finals and because it would only sit on 4-player tables
in the preliminary rounds.

That make any sense?

Josh

Messages.Author: Flux
Messages.Body:
Wouter Kuyper wrote:

> but then the next question: Do we want the size of the tournament to
> play a role in your choice of deck? Should the size of the tournament
> favour some deck-types?
>
> W

I think few people will say yes to that. The number of decks that can do
well at a tournament should be as large as possible, so as to give the
players more choices and keep the game dynamic.

The 'problem' with large tournaments is that they make Game Wins
redundant. You get back to the pre-GW situation, where VPs are all that
really matters, and so the 'old' sweep-the-table heavy bleed decks
dominate (no pun intended).

IMO, the 'best' way to avoid this as much as possible (given the
currents rules) would be to have more rounds in large tournaments, so
sweep decks would have more of an opportunity to find their counter and
miss a few tables, and other decks could get some more GWs. Of course,
organizing a 100-person-3+f-round-tournament seems hard enough, adding
more rounds can't make it any easier... :)

Flux
